title: Replication mode
blurb: Paste a paper's claim; it is rebuilt on our data and judged, including decay after publication.
honesty: Skeptic reduces false discoveries and quantifies uncertainty. It does not prove truth.
Null-world validity depends on the null generator preserving the data's real structure (assumptions are listed per generator).
Backtests are not forecasts. Nothing here is trading advice.

Built on known methods: White's Reality Check, Hansen's SPA, Deflated Sharpe, Benjamini-Hochberg, alpha-investing (Foster & Stine). Our contribution is applying them to an autonomous agent's own search as one integrated, measurable system.

papers.title: Short-Term Trading and Stock Return Anomalies: Momentum, Reversal, and Share Issuance
papers.abstract: Abstract This article examines how the extent of short-term trading relates to the efficiency of stock prices. We employ a new duration measure based on quarterly institutional investors’ portfolio holdings, next to existing proxies such as trading volume, the percentage of transient institutions, and fund turnover. Momentum returns and subsequent returns reversal are generally much stronger for stocks held primarily by short-term investors, especially if these investors recently had superior recent performance which could make them overconfident. Our results point toward the behavioral theory

papers.venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
papers.abstract: Price declines over the previous quarter lead to stronger reversals across the subsequent 2 months. papers.title: Short-term reversals, returns to liquidity provision and the costs of immediacy*
papers.abstract: Some mutual funds act as contrarian traders, earning returns in the stock market by providing liquidity, while others demand liquidity and suffer costs of immediacy. High market beta funds, large cap funds, and funds exposed to momentum suffer over 2.5% pa. in costs of immediacy.
